issues.detail: The Greek 'εν' (en) means 'in', but the Vietnamese 'Chỉ có' translates to 'Only have/There is only'. This changes the meaning from being 'in one body' to 'having only one body'.
The Greek 'καθως' (kathos) functions as 'as' or 'just as', but the Vietnamese 'như' is used here in a way that slightly weakens the comparative structure of the original.
